{"id": "a38307b1-04bf-4436-92f4-cd4fde635f76", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_I0rplivNJN5VPFz5LuAbIn", "content": "[{'text': '{\"content\": \"---\\\\nname: llmops-sagemaker-training\\\\ndescription: Diagnose an Amazon SageMaker training or customization job, including Nova and JumpStart fine-tuning,\\\\n  that fails, errors, hangs or never starts. Use this skill when a training job is denied access to S3, a\\\\n  KMS key or iam:PassRole, fails with InsufficientInstanceCapacity, ResourceLimitExceeded or out of\\\\n  memory, goes to Failed with no logs, starts over after a spot interruption or ignores its checkpoints,\\\\n  stalls as a multi-node run, times out in VPC mode, finds no input files, hides its loss metrics, does\\\\n  not reuse its warm pool, or bills GPU time for a run that produced no model, even if they do not mention\\\\n  execution roles, key policies, checkpoint paths, metric definitions, security groups or data channels by\\\\n  name. It also reviews training-job health. Findings carry LLM-SM-TRAIN check-ids with a severity and an\\\\n  AWS-doc citation, from read-only APIs.\\\\nmetadata:\\\\n  author: user-g\\\\n  version: \\\\\"1.0.0\\\\\"\\\\n  summary: \\\\\"Diagnoses Amazon SageMaker training and fine-tuning jobs that fail, hang, never start, or waste GPU time.\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: \\\\\"CHAT\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.aws-services: \\\\\"Amazon SageMaker AI, Amazon S3, Amazon CloudWatch\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.technical-domains: \\\\\"AI/ML\\\\\"\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n# LLMOps \\\\u2014 SageMaker training / customization jobs\\\\n\\\\nYou diagnose **Amazon SageMaker training and customization jobs** for a GenAI workload \\\\u2014 Nova\\\\nfine-tuning/SFT/LoRA recipes and JumpStart fine-tuning. Your job is a **read-only failure review**:\\\\nwhen a job fails, stalls, or will not start, exactly which catalog check fired and what the operator\\\\nshould run to fix it \\\\u2014 and, just as important, telling a true failure apart from a job that is merely\\\\nwaiting on capacity.\\\\n\\\\nThis skill belongs to the **`llmops-agent`** custom agent and is **fully self-contained**: everything\\\\nit needs is in this package\\'s `references/` and `assets/`. It has **no dependency on any other\\\\nskill**. The route-outs in *When NOT to Use* are handoffs, not imports.\\\\n\\\\nEvery finding is grounded in the **LLM-SM** check family under\\\\n[checks-sagemaker-training.md](references/checks-sagemaker-training.md) \\\\u2014 the `LLM-SM-TRAIN-*` sub-family for training /\\\\ncustomization; load it before assigning any check-id or severity. Each finding carries a stable `check-id`, a severity, and an AWS-doc citation. You\\\\nnever invent a threshold: a tuning judgment with no AWS-published number is marked `workload-specific`\\\\nand reported as `INFO`, while a binary failed/absent state keeps its catalog severity. This skill uses\\\\n**read-only APIs only** \\\\u2014 it never mutates a resource.\\\\n\\\\n## When to Use\\\\n\\\\nActivate this skill when the user:\\\\n\\\\n- Says a **Nova SFT+LoRA (or JumpStart) training/customization job failed or is stuck** and wants to\\\\n  know why.\\\\n- Reports **corrupt or malformed training data** \\\\u2014 a Bedrock Converse JSONL that does not parse, a\\\\n  wrong schema, or the invalid-sample tolerance exceeded.\\\\n- Reports a job that **will not start** \\\\u2014 `InsufficientInstanceCapacity`, a training instance quota of\\\\n  zero, or a job **stuck Pending on capacity**.\\\\n- Reports a **recipe / hyperparameter validation error**, an **IAM/S3 access** failure on the\\\\n  training or recipe data, or an **empty / misconfigured data channel**.\\\\n- Asks whether a **completed** job actually produced a **checkpoint**, or about **GPU cost billed for a\\\\n  failed or empty run**.\\\\n- Wants a **health report** for one or more training/customization jobs.\\\\n\\\\n## When NOT to Use\\\\n\\\\nThis skill covers **SageMaker training / customization jobs** only. Route elsewhere (handoffs, not\\\\ndependencies):\\\\n\\\\n- **Real-time inference endpoints** \\\\u2192 `llmops-sagemaker-inference-endpoints`.\\\\n- **Serverless or asynchronous inference** \\\\u2192 `llmops-sagemaker-serverless-async`.\\\\n- **Batch transform / offline scoring** \\\\u2192 `llmops-sagemaker-batch`.\\\\n- **SageMaker-side evaluation jobs** \\\\u2192 `llmops-sagemaker-evaluation`.\\\\n- **Model Registry approval / lineage for a customized artifact** \\\\u2192 `llmops-sagemaker-model-registry`.\\\\n- **Bedrock model / invocation config** \\\\u2192 `llmops-bedrock-configuration`.\\\\n- **Bedrock Guardrails** \\\\u2192 `llmops-guardrails`.\\\\n- **Bedrock quota and token / inference cost** \\\\u2192 `llmops-capacity-cost`.\\\\n- **Knowledge bases / RAG ingestion & retrieval** \\\\u2192 `llmops-rag-knowledge`.\\\\n- **Bedrock Agents and AgentCore runtime** \\\\u2192 `llmops-agent-runtime`.\\\\n- **A live incident \\\\u2014 \\\\\"is this AWS or me?\\\\\"** \\\\u2192 `llmops-incident-triage`.\\\\n- **Bedrock-native model evaluation (`CreateEvaluationJob`)** \\\\u2192 `llmops-quality-evaluation`.\\\\n- **Future price quotes** \\\\u2192 the [AWS Pricing Calculator](https://calculator.aws/).\\\\n\\\\n## The LLM-SM Check Family\\\\n\\\\nGrounded in [checks-sagemaker-training.md](references/checks-sagemaker-training.md); load it when a symptom matches a row below. Match the symptom, confirm with the collection\\\\ncalls, then report with the check-id and severity from the catalog. The full six-column detection\\\\nrules, remediations, and citations live in the reference \\\\u2014 the table below is a what-it-catches index.\\\\n\\\\n**Training / customization (LLM-SM-TRAIN-*):**\\\\n\\\\n| check-id | severity | what it catches |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| LLM-SM-TRAIN-001 | HIGH | Job `Failed` on malformed/corrupt training data (JSONL parse, missing keys, invalid-sample tolerance exceeded). |\\\\n| LLM-SM-TRAIN-002 | HIGH | `InsufficientInstanceCapacity` \\\\u2014 AWS-side GPU shortfall (retry/alternate, not a quota fix). |\\\\n| LLM-SM-TRAIN-003 | HIGH | Training instance-type service quota = 0 \\\\u2014 customer quota (request an increase). |\\\\n| LLM-SM-TRAIN-004 | HIGH | Recipe/hyperparameter validation failure (null or out-of-range `HyperParameters`). |\\\\n| LLM-SM-TRAIN-005 | HIGH | Execution-role `AccessDenied` on the training/recipe/output S3 (or KMS). |\\\\n| LLM-SM-TRAIN-006 | HIGH | Empty or wrong-URI input data channel. |\\\\n| LLM-SM-TRAIN-007 | MEDIUM | Job `InProgress`/`Pending` on capacity \\\\u2014 **not** Failed; a false-positive trap. |\\\\n| LLM-SM-TRAIN-008 | HIGH | Job `Completed` but no checkpoint at the output path \\\\u2014 billed, unusable. |\\\\n\\\\nLoad [checks-sagemaker-training.md](references/checks-sagemaker-training.md) before writing any finding: it holds the full detection rules, remediations, and citations.\\\\n\\\\n## Router\\\\n\\\\nHow to read each API and signal is in [collection-reference.md](references/collection-reference.md). Load it with any row.\\\\n\\\\n| Operator says | First read | Load |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| My training job failed, the data looks corrupt or won\\'t parse | `DescribeTrainingJob` `FailureReason`, then the JSONL sample | [checks-sagemaker-training.md](references/checks-sagemaker-training.md) (LLM-SM-TRAIN-001), [api-quirks.md](references/api-quirks.md) |\\\\n| The job won\\'t start, there\\'s no GPU capacity | `DescribeTrainingJob` `FailureReason` and `SecondaryStatus` | [checks-sagemaker-training.md](references/checks-sagemaker-training.md) (LLM-SM-TRAIN-002, 003), [api-quirks.md](references/api-quirks.md) |\\\\n| It says the quota is exceeded, do I need a quota increase | `service-quotas get-service-quota` for the training instance type | [checks-sagemaker-training.md](references/checks-sagemaker-training.md) (LLM-SM-TRAIN-003) |\\\\n| The recipe or hyperparameters were rejected | `DescribeTrainingJob` `HyperParameters` and the S3 recipe object | [checks-sagemaker-training.md](references/checks-sagemaker-training.md) (LLM-SM-TRAIN-004), [api-quirks.md](references/api-quirks.md) |\\\\n| The job got access denied on S3 or KMS | `DescribeTrainingJob` `RoleArn`, then `iam:SimulatePrincipalPolicy` on the data and output prefixes | [checks-sagemaker-training.md](references/checks-sagemaker-training.md) (LLM-SM-TRAIN-005) |\\\\n| The job ran but read no data, the channel is empty | `InputDataConfig` S3 URIs, then `ListObjectsV2` on each prefix | [checks-sagemaker-training.md](references/checks-sagemaker-training.md) (LLM-SM-TRAIN-006) |\\\\n| The job has been Pending for hours, is it broken | `TrainingJobStatus` and `SecondaryStatus` | [api-quirks.md](references/api-quirks.md) \\\\u00a71 (LLM-SM-TRAIN-007) |\\\\n| It says Completed but I can\\'t find the model | `ModelArtifacts.S3ModelArtifacts`, then `HeadObject` | [checks-sagemaker-training.md](references/checks-sagemaker-training.md) (LLM-SM-TRAIN-008), [metrics-and-logs.md](references/metrics-and-logs.md) |\\\\n| Why was I billed for a run that gave nothing | `BillableTimeInSeconds`, status and artifact check | [checks-sagemaker-training.md](references/checks-sagemaker-training.md) (LLM-SM-TRAIN-002, 007, 008) |\\\\n\\\\n## Break-fix first\\\\n\\\\nWhen the user states a specific error or symptom (an access denied, a PassRole or KMS error, a\\\\ncapacity or quota error, out of memory, no logs, a spot restart, a checkpoint that does not resume, a\\\\nhang, missing metrics), answer that error before any health review:\\\\n\\\\n- Load [known-causes.md](references/known-causes.md) whenever the user names an error or symptom;\\\\n  match it to a section, check the cited AWS page, and give the cause, how to confirm it, and the fix.\\\\n- Answer in this turn. Do not end with only a plan or \\\\\"I\\'ll report back\\\\\"; if you also inspect the\\\\n  account, include what you found and what you could not read.\\\\n- A known cause tied to an `LLM-SM-TRAIN-*` id is a finding with the catalog severity. A cause with no\\\\n  id is guidance with its AWS citation; never invent an id for it.\\\\n- Run the Review Procedure below only when asked for a review or when there are jobs to inspect.\\\\n\\\\n## Review Procedure\\\\n\\\\nThe most common live request. Classify **before** prescribing anything. Run the steps in order and\\\\ntrack progress against this checklist. Every step is **best-effort**: if an API is denied or a feature\\\\nis unsupported in the region, record that signal as **unavailable** and continue.\\\\n\\\\n- [ ] Step 1: `ListTrainingJobs` / `DescribeTrainingJob` (a Nova customization job runs as a\\\\n  recipe-driven training job \\\\u2014 describe it by its training-job name) for `TrainingJobStatus`,\\\\n  `SecondaryStatus`, and `FailureReason`.\\\\n- [ ] Step 2: Classify Pending-vs-Failed. If the job is `InProgress` with `SecondaryStatus`\\\\n  `Starting`/`Pending` waiting on capacity, it is **NOT** Failed (`api-quirks.md` \\\\u00a71, LLM-SM-TRAIN-007)\\\\n  \\\\u2014 report the true status and **stop here**; prescribe no config change.\\\\n- [ ] Step 3: If `Failed`, bucket the `FailureReason` into exactly one cause and cite the check:\\\\n  malformed data (LLM-SM-TRAIN-001) / AWS-side capacity (LLM-SM-TRAIN-002) / customer quota = 0,\\\\n  cross-checking `service-quotas get-service-quota` (LLM-SM-TRAIN-003) / recipe-hyperparameter\\\\n  (LLM-SM-TRAIN-004) / IAM-S3 (LLM-SM-TRAIN-005) / empty-or-wrong channel URI (LLM-SM-TRAIN-006). The\\\\n  capacity-vs-quota split is opposite remediations \\\\u2014 read **both** the `FailureReason` and the quota\\\\n  value (`api-quirks.md` \\\\u00a72).\\\\n- [ ] Step 4: If `Completed`, confirm an artifact exists \\\\u2014 `s3:HeadObject`/`ListObjectsV2` on\\\\n  `ModelArtifacts.S3ModelArtifacts` / the recipe output path. A succeeded job with no checkpoint is\\\\n  LLM-SM-TRAIN-008. Note that `allow_percentage_invalid_samples` can let a job `Complete` while\\\\n  silently dropping corrupt records (`api-quirks.md` \\\\u00a73) \\\\u2014 a \\\\\"success\\\\\" is not proof all data was used.\\\\n- [ ] Step 5: Note billed GPU cost for any failed, empty, or stalled run (LLM-SM-TRAIN-002/007/008).\\\\n\\\\nProduce the result in one turn; disclose any job, region, or S3 prefix you could not read. Use\\\\n[training-job-health-report-template.md](assets/training-job-health-report-template.md) when a full report is requested.\\\\n\\\\n## Before You Present \\\\u2014 Validate Your Own Output\\\\n\\\\nA wrong or unsupported finding is worse than a slow one. Before presenting, re-check your output\\\\nagainst this list. Treat it as a gate, not a suggestion.\\\\n\\\\n- [ ] Every finding carries a matching **`check-id`** from [checks-sagemaker-training.md](references/checks-sagemaker-training.md) (load it if any id is unconfirmed),\\\\n  and that id corresponds to what was actually observed \\\\u2014 not a near-miss id reused for convenience.\\\\n- [ ] Every cited value was **actually observed, not inferred**. A training job that is\\\\n  `InProgress`/`Pending` on capacity is **never reported as a failure** (load [api-quirks.md](references/api-quirks.md)\\\\n  \\\\u00a71 if the job is not `Failed`, LLM-SM-TRAIN-007).\\\\n- [ ] A **training-failure classification** names exactly one bucket with its `LLM-SM-TRAIN-*` id, and\\\\n  a capacity-vs-quota call reads **both** the `FailureReason` and the `service-quotas` value (\\\\u00a72).\\\\n- [ ] No severity was invented \\\\u2014 each matches the catalog; a tuning threshold AWS does not publish is\\\\n  marked `workload-specific` / `INFO`, while a binary failed/absent state keeps its catalog severity.\\\\n- [ ] **No mutating API was called or implied as done.** Remediations are phrased as recommendations\\\\n  with the exact command for the operator to run.\\\\n- [ ] No **raw 12-digit AWS account ID** and no **secret value** (including raw training-data content)\\\\n  appear anywhere \\\\u2014 env vars are referenced by key name only.\\\\n- [ ] The jobs, regions, and S3 prefixes **not** covered are disclosed, with the reason.\\\\n- [ ] When a full report is requested, the output follows\\\\n  [training-job-health-report-template.md](assets/training-job-health-report-template.md).\\\\n\\\\nIf any item cannot be satisfied, say so explicitly in the output rather than quietly dropping it.\\\\n\\\\n## Guardrails\\\\n\\\\nNon-negotiable, at every step:\\\\n\\\\n1. **Read-only.** Never call a training mutation (`CreateTrainingJob`, `StopTrainingJob`) or any other\\\\n   mutating API. Recommend the fix and give the exact CLI/IaC command; let the user run it.\\\\n2. **Never echo a raw AWS account ID.** Refer to the account by alias or as `the account under\\\\n   review`. If an ARN must be quoted as evidence, mask the account segment\\\\n   (`arn:aws:sagemaker:us-east-1:<account>:training-job/...`). The same applies to anything\\\\n   credential-shaped.\\\\n3. **Never disclose secret material.** Report environment variables, keys, tokens, connection strings,\\\\n   and raw training-data content by **key name / reference only** \\\\u2014 never the value, never a partial\\\\n   value.\\\\n4. **Evidence or silence.** Every finding cites the concrete value that triggered it. Distinguish a\\\\n   true `Failed` from a Pending-on-capacity job (load [api-quirks.md](references/api-quirks.md) \\\\u00a71 whenever a job is not\\\\n   `Failed`).\\\\n5. **A check-id on every finding.** Each finding references an LLM-SM `check-id` and carries that\\\\n   check\\'s severity and AWS-doc citation. No freelance findings. A documented cause\\\\n   from known-causes.md that has no check-id is labelled guidance with its citation, not a finding.\\\\n6. **Never invent a threshold.** Severities come from the catalog. No AWS-published number \\\\u2192 `INFO`,\\\\n   marked `workload-specific`.\\\\n7. **Bound the work and disclose what you skipped.** State which jobs, regions, or checks you did not\\\\n   cover, and why (budget, permissions, region-unsupported feature).\\\\n\\\\n## Common wrong answers\\\\n- \\\\\"The job is `InProgress` with `Pending`, so it is failing.\\\\\" A job waiting on GPU capacity is control-plane-healthy, not `Failed`. Report the true status and prescribe no config change (`api-quirks.md` \\\\u00a71, LLM-SM-TRAIN-007).\\\\n- \\\\\"It won\\'t get instances, so request a quota increase.\\\\\" `InsufficientInstanceCapacity` is an AWS-side shortfall and the fix is retry or an alternate instance type or region; a quota of zero is a customer limit and needs `request-service-quota-increase`. Read both the `FailureReason` and `service-quotas get-service-quota` before choosing (`api-quirks.md` \\\\u00a72, LLM-SM-TRAIN-002, 003).\\\\n- \\\\\"The job `Completed`, so all the training data was used.\\\\\" With an invalid-sample tolerance such as `allow_percentage_invalid_samples`, corrupt records are silently dropped and the job still completes. Check the drop count in the log, not just the status (`api-quirks.md` \\\\u00a73, LLM-SM-TRAIN-001).\\\\n- \\\\\"A required hyperparameter was left out, so it falls back to a default.\\\\\" Nova rejects a null or omitted required `HyperParameters` value at create time. It is a hard validation failure (`api-quirks.md` \\\\u00a74, LLM-SM-TRAIN-004).\\\\n- \\\\\"The recipe error is in the launch call parameter.\\\\\" Recipes are passed by S3 reference because the inline field is capped near 2500 characters. Inspect the S3 recipe object and confirm the execution role can read it (`api-quirks.md` \\\\u00a75, LLM-SM-TRAIN-004, 005, 006).\\\\n- \\\\\"A collection call returned AccessDenied, so the check doesn\\'t apply.\\\\\" AccessDenied is a gap, not a clean result. Name the API and resource you could not read, continue, and disclose the gap.\\\\n## Severity Definitions\\\\n\\\\n| Severity | Meaning | Response SLA (derived) |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| **CRITICAL** | Active production impact or total review blindness | 24\\\\u201348 hours |\\\\n| **HIGH** | Serious reliability / security / cost risk | Within 1 week |\\\\n| **MEDIUM** | Meaningful gap vs best practice | Within 30 days |\\\\n| **LOW** | Minor hardening | When convenient |\\\\n| **INFO** | Observation with no AWS-published threshold | N/A \\\\u2014 document / monitor |\\\\n\\\\nSLAs are operational guidance (derived), not AWS-published commitments.\\\\n\\\\n## Error Handling\\\\n\\\\nBefore interpreting any response, consult [api-quirks.md](references/api-quirks.md) \\\\u2014 it enumerates the misleading\\\\nread-only responses that cause false positives and false negatives in this review (traps \\\\u00a71\\\\u2013\\\\u00a75):\\\\n\\\\n- **`InProgress`/`SecondaryStatus Pending` is NOT `Failed`** (\\\\u00a71). A job waiting on GPU capacity is\\\\n  control-plane-healthy; report Pending-on-capacity and prescribe no config change (LLM-SM-TRAIN-007).\\\\n- **`InsufficientInstanceCapacity` (AWS-side) \\\\u2260 instance-type quota = 0 (customer)** (\\\\u00a72). Opposite\\\\n  remediations \\\\u2014 retry/alternate for capacity (LLM-SM-TRAIN-002) vs a quota-increase request for a\\\\n  zero quota (LLM-SM-TRAIN-003). Read both the `FailureReason` and `service-quotas get-service-quota`.\\\\n- **`allow_percentage_invalid_samples` silently drops records** (\\\\u00a73). A job can report `Completed`\\\\n  while dropping corrupt JSONL up to the tolerance \\\\u2014 \\\\\"succeeded\\\\\" is not proof all data was used\\\\n  (LLM-SM-TRAIN-001). Check the drop count, not just the status.\\\\n- **Nova rejects a null `HyperParameters` map** (\\\\u00a74). A null/omitted required hyperparameter is a\\\\n  hard validation failure at create time, not a silent default (LLM-SM-TRAIN-004).\\\\n- **The recipe is referenced from S3, not inlined** (\\\\u00a75). The inline field is capped (~2500 chars),\\\\n  so a recipe error points at the **S3 recipe object** and the role must be able to read it\\\\n  (LLM-SM-TRAIN-004/005/006).\\\\n\\\\nOperational failures: on **AccessDenied** for a collection call, report the specific API and resource\\\\nyou could not read, continue with the rest, and list the gap \\\\u2014 never guess. On a **region unsupported\\\\nfor a feature**, record it as a disclosed assumption, not a finding. On **throttling of describe/list\\\\ncalls**, back off and paginate. On **ambiguous scope**, ask or default to the caller\\'s current region\\\\nand the jobs in it, and say so.\\\\n\\\\n## Appendix \\\\u2014 Reference Links\\\\n\\\\nReferences under `references/`:\\\\n\\\\n- [checks-sagemaker-training.md](references/checks-sagemaker-training.md) \\\\u2014 load before assigning any check-id or severity: the\\\\n  LLM-SM-TRAIN-* check catalog (primary).\\\\n- [collection-reference.md](references/collection-reference.md) \\\\u2014 load with any Router row, or when you need the read-only SM-family\\\\n  collection API (training describe, service-quotas, S3-read, IAM-read) and the fields each contributes.\\\\n- [metrics-and-logs.md](references/metrics-and-logs.md) \\\\u2014 load when mapping a `FailureReason` to a TRAIN check or reading the\\\\n  training-job describe/log signals, including the EventBridge lifecycle note for one-shot jobs.\\\\n- [api-quirks.md](references/api-quirks.md) \\\\u2014 load before interpreting any status, `FailureReason` or quota value:\\\\n  misleading read-only API responses (traps \\\\u00a71\\\\u2013\\\\u00a75).\\\\n- [known-causes.md](references/known-causes.md) \\\\u2014 load whenever the user names a specific error or\\\\n  symptom: documented break-fix causes (PassRole vs execution role, KMS key policy, missing logs,\\\\n  capacity vs quota, spot and checkpoint resume, host vs GPU memory, distributed and VPC networking,\\\\n  metric definitions), each with its AWS-doc citation.\\\\n\\\\nOutput template under `assets/`:\\\\n\\\\n- {"id": "8a4a1a27-16d9-45c3-8b20-f2fa1ae5cd21", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_KW1cO2SOOgdKNebllSIE1p", "content": "[{'text': '# API Quirks\\n\\nSageMaker read-only API responses whose obvious reading is **wrong** or misleading for a training / customization job review (traps \u00a71\u2013\u00a75). Each entry: the trap, why it misleads, and the correct interpretation. Misreading these produces false positives (phantom findings) or false negatives (missed CRITICALs).\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 1. SageMaker training `InProgress` / `SecondaryStatus Pending` is NOT `Failed`\\n\\n- **Trap:** A training/customization job that has not started training yet \u2014 `TrainingJobStatus: InProgress` with `SecondaryStatus: Starting`/`Pending` while it waits on GPU capacity \u2014 reads to an impatient operator as \"failing\", and gets reported as a failure.\\n- **Correct reading:** A job waiting on capacity is **control-plane-healthy**, not failed. Reporting it as a failure is a false positive. Report the true Pending-on-capacity status and prescribe **no** config change for a job that has not failed (LLM-SM-TRAIN-007). Only a `TrainingJobStatus: Failed` with a `FailureReason` is a failure.\\n\\n## 2. `InsufficientInstanceCapacity` \u2260 a quota problem\\n\\n- **Trap:** Any \"the job won\\'t get instances\" symptom reads as \"request a quota increase.\"\\n- **Correct reading:** `InsufficientInstanceCapacity` is an **AWS-side** shortfall of the GPU instance type at that moment; a service quota of **zero** for the instance type is a **customer** limit. The remediations are **opposite** \u2014 retry/alternate instance or region for capacity (LLM-SM-TRAIN-002) versus `request-service-quota-increase` for a zero quota (LLM-SM-TRAIN-003). Distinguish by reading **both** the `FailureReason` and `service-quotas get-service-quota`; a quota increase does nothing for a capacity shortfall, and a retry does nothing for a zero quota.\\n\\n## 3. `allow_percentage_invalid_samples` silently drops records\\n\\n- **Trap:** A customization job that reports `Completed` reads as \"all training data was used.\"\\n- **Correct reading:** When the recipe sets an invalid-sample tolerance (e.g. `allow_percentage_invalid_samples`), the job can **drop** malformed records up to that tolerance and still report `Completed` \u2014 the model trained on **less data than intended**. `Completed` \u2260 \"all data used\". Check the drop count / training log, not just the status, before trusting a run; a few corrupt JSONL lines can be silently dropped rather than failing the job (LLM-SM-TRAIN-001).\\n\\n## 4. Nova customization rejects a null `HyperParameters` map\\n\\n- **Trap:** An omitted or null required hyperparameter reads as \"it will fall back to a default.\"\\n- **Correct reading:** A Nova customization job **rejects a null/omitted required `HyperParameters` value at create/validate time** \u2014 it is a hard validation failure, not a \"use the default.\" Supply every required value, none null, within the documented range (LLM-SM-TRAIN-004).\\n\\n## 5. The recipe is referenced from S3, not inlined (~2500-char cap)\\n\\n- **Trap:** A recipe error reads as a malformed API parameter to fix in the launch call.\\n- **Correct reading:** Nova/JumpStart recipes are passed **by S3 reference** because the inline hyperparameter field is capped (~2500 chars). A recipe error therefore points at the **S3 recipe object**, not the API parameter \u2014 inspect the object itself, and confirm the execution role can **read** it (ties to LLM-SM-TRAIN-004 / 005 / 006).\\n'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_n1u5s6xscoejz0rqv4aB8F", "content": "[{'text': '# Known Causes \u2014 SageMaker training break-fix\\n\\nDocumented causes for the training errors operators report most, for answering a stated error\\ndirectly (SKILL.md, *Break-fix first*). Each bullet names the AWS page it rests on; verify against\\nthat page before you answer. A cause tied to an `LLM-SM-TRAIN-*` id is reported as that finding with\\nthe catalog severity; a cause with no id is **guidance**, cited by URL, never given an invented id.\\nWhere AWS says nothing, say so rather than filling the gap.\\n\\n## 1. Access errors \u2014 which identity, which policy\\n\\n- **`not authorized to perform: iam:PassRole` when creating the job** is the *caller\\'s* permission, not the execution role\\'s: whoever calls `CreateTrainingJob` must be allowed `iam:PassRole` on the role it passes, usually scoped with `iam:PassedToService` = `sagemaker.amazonaws.com`. Fix the caller\\'s policy, not the execution role ([troubleshooting IAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/security_iam_troubleshoot.html), [passing roles](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/sagemaker-roles.html)).\\n- **S3 access denied although the execution role \"has S3\"** \u2014 the `CreateTrainingJob` execution role needs `s3:ListBucket` on the input bucket and `s3:GetObject`/`s3:PutObject` on the input and output prefixes, plus `kms:Decrypt` when the input is SSE-KMS encrypted; check the bucket policy as well as the role (LLM-SM-TRAIN-005) ([CreateTrainingJob execution role](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/sagemaker-roles.html)).\\n- **KMS error although the role\\'s IAM policy allows `kms:Decrypt`/`GenerateDataKey`** \u2014 an IAM policy has no effect on a KMS key unless the key policy allows it; for `OutputDataConfig.KmsKeyId` AWS states the key policy must grant the role you pass to `CreateTrainingJob`. Add a key-policy statement naming the execution role ARN with the needed actions, or confirm the key policy delegates to IAM (LLM-SM-TRAIN-005) ([key policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/key-policies.html), [OutputDataConfig](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/APIReference/API_OutputDataConfig.html)).\\n- **An output or volume key also needs its own action** \u2014 AWS lists `kms:Encrypt` for an output key and `kms:CreateGrant` for a volume key on the training execution role ([CreateTrainingJob execution role](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/sagemaker-roles.html)).\\n\\n## 2. Failed fast with no CloudWatch logs\\n\\n- **Read `FailureReason` first**, then the log group `/aws/sagemaker/TrainingJobs` (streams `[training-job-name]/algo-[n]-[timestamp]`) ([DescribeTrainingJob](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/API_DescribeTrainingJob.html), [log groups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/logging-cloudwatch.html)).\\n- **No log stream at all is also what an execution role without CloudWatch Logs permissions looks like** \u2014 AWS\\'s training-role policy includes `logs:CreateLogGroup`, `logs:CreateLogStream`, `logs:PutLogEvents` and `logs:DescribeLogStreams`; check them before concluding the container never started ([CreateTrainingJob execution role](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/sagemaker-roles.html)).\\n- **An image the role cannot pull** fails before any training code runs \u2014 the same policy lists `ecr:GetAuthorizationToken`, `ecr:BatchCheckLayerAvailability`, `ecr:GetDownloadUrlForLayer` and `ecr:BatchGetImage` for the training image repository ([CreateTrainingJob execution role](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/sagemaker-roles.html)).\\n\\n## 3. Capacity versus quota\\n\\n- **`ResourceLimitExceeded` is an account resource limit** \u2014 request an increase through Service Quotas (LLM-SM-TRAIN-003) ([CreateTrainingJob errors](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/APIReference/API_CreateTrainingJob.html), [quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/regions-quotas.html)).\\n- **`InsufficientInstanceCapacity` means AWS lacks capacity for that request at that moment**; EC2 documents retrying after a few minutes, requesting fewer instances, or using a different instance type. A quota increase does not add capacity \u2014 this skill\\'s reading, consistent with the catalog row (LLM-SM-TRAIN-002) ([EC2 insufficient capacity](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/troubleshooting-launch.html)).\\n\\n## 4. Spot interruptions and checkpoints that do not resume\\n\\n- **Managed spot needs `EnableManagedSpotTraining` and `MaxWaitTimeInSeconds` larger than `MaxRuntimeInSeconds`**; AWS recommends checkpointing for anything but short jobs, and algorithms that cannot checkpoint are capped at a 3600-second wait ([managed spot training](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-managed-spot-training.html)).\\n- **Writing checkpoints is not resuming from them.** SageMaker syncs the local checkpoint directory (default `/opt/ml/checkpoints`) with the checkpoint S3 URI you configure and copies existing checkpoints back into the container at job start; a custom script must save to that local path *and load from it* on start, otherwise it starts from scratch ([checkpoints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-checkpoints.html)).\\n- **Checkpoints added to S3 after the job started are not copied into the running container** \u2014 only what exists at start is restored ([checkpoints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-checkpoints.html)).\\n\\n## 5. Out of memory partway through\\n\\n- **Tell host memory from GPU memory before resizing**: `/aws/sagemaker/TrainingJobs` publishes `MemoryUtilization` (container memory) and `GPUMemoryUtilization` (summed across GPUs, so 0\u2013400% on four GPUs) per `[job]/algo-[n]` host; the one that peaks before the failure names the resource to scale ([job metrics](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/monitoring-cloudwatch.html)).\\n\\n## 6. Distributed or VPC-mode jobs that hang or time out\\n\\n- **Multi-node jobs in a VPC need a security-group rule allowing inbound traffic between members of the same security group**, and EFA-enabled instances need both inbound and outbound all-traffic rules within the group; single-node runs never exercise this path ([training in a VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/train-vpc.html)).\\n- **A VPC with no internet access has no route to S3 or other services** unless you create an Amazon S3 VPC endpoint, interface VPC endpoints for other AWS services, or a NAT gateway for services and resources without one ([training in a VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/train-vpc.html)).\\n\\n## 7. Loss curve printed to stdout but not in the console\\n\\n- **SageMaker only publishes custom training metrics it is told to parse**: define `MetricDefinitions` (a name plus a regular expression) in `AlgorithmSpecification`, and make sure the regex matches the exact log line the script writes ([define training metrics](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/define-train-metrics.html)).\\n'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_8ctI6FldkYxhiWqd14buCy", "content": "[{'text': '# Checks \u2014 SageMaker training / fine-tuning / customization jobs (LLM-SM-TRAIN-*)\\n\\nCovers Amazon SageMaker training jobs that customize an LLM \u2014 Nova fine-tuning/SFT/LoRA recipes and JumpStart fine-tuning.\\n\\nEach row: `check-id | pillar | severity | detection-rule | remediation | AWS-doc-citation`\\n\\nFamily code: **SM** = SageMaker for LLMs. Family prefix: `LLM-SM-`; the `LLM-SM-TRAIN-*` sub-family covers training / customization.\\n\\nSeverity scale: CRITICAL > HIGH > MEDIUM > LOW > INFO. A *tuning or right-sizing judgment* with no AWS-published number is marked `workload-specific` at severity INFO; a *binary present/absent/failed* state (a job FAILED, no checkpoint produced, access denied) keeps its catalog severity even when AWS publishes no number.\\n\\n## Training / fine-tuning / customization jobs (LLM-SM-TRAIN-*)\\n\\nCovers SageMaker training jobs that customize an LLM \u2014 Nova fine-tuning/SFT/LoRA recipes and JumpStart fine-tuning. One check per distinct failure mode; a failed, empty, or stalled GPU run is billed, so the cost consequence is noted inside TRAIN-002/007/008 rather than as a separate row.\\n\\n| check-id | pillar | severity | detection-rule | remediation | AWS-doc-citation |\\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\\n| LLM-SM-TRAIN-001 | Reliability | HIGH | `DescribeTrainingJob` / customization job `TrainingJobStatus` = `Failed` with a `FailureReason` indicating malformed or corrupt training data \u2014 Bedrock Converse JSONL that does not parse, a record missing required `messages`/`role`/`content` keys, or the invalid-sample count exceeding the recipe\\'s tolerance. The failure is in the **data**, not capacity. | Validate every JSONL record against the Converse fine-tuning schema offline before resubmitting; fix or drop the malformed records; if the recipe exposes an invalid-sample tolerance, confirm the real drop rate rather than raising the tolerance to mask corrupt data. | https://docs.aws.amazon.com/nova/latest/userguide/fine-tune-prepare-data-understanding.html |\\n| LLM-SM-TRAIN-002 | Reliability | HIGH | Job `Failed`/stuck with `FailureReason` or secondary status showing `InsufficientInstanceCapacity` for the requested GPU instance type \u2014 an **AWS-side** capacity shortfall, not a customer misconfiguration. | Do not change the recipe or request a quota increase. Retry with backoff, try an alternate GPU instance type or a different AZ/region the recipe supports, or schedule off-peak. Classify as service-side (see api-quirks capacity trap). Note the GPU time billed for the failed launch. | https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/your-algorithms-training-algo-running-container.html |\\n| LLM-SM-TRAIN-003 | Cost Optimization | HIGH | Job `Failed` with `ResourceLimitExceeded` / an instance-type service quota of **zero** for the requested training instance \u2014 a **customer quota** problem distinct from AWS capacity (TRAIN-002). `service-quotas get-service-quota` returns `Value` 0 for that `sagemaker` training-usage quota. | Request a quota increase for the specific SageMaker training instance type via `aws service-quotas request-service-quota-increase --service-code sagemaker --quota-code <code> --desired-value <n>`; distinguish from InsufficientInstanceCapacity which no quota change fixes. | https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/sagemaker.html |\\n| LLM-SM-TRAIN-004 | Operational Excellence | HIGH | Job `Failed` with a `FailureReason` citing recipe or hyperparameter validation \u2014 a null/omitted required `HyperParameters` value Nova rejects, an out-of-range value, or a malformed recipe reference. Config error, not data or capacity. | Correct the recipe/hyperparameters against the published Nova customization recipe spec (supply all required values, none null, within documented ranges) and resubmit; validate the recipe locally before launch. | https://docs.aws.amazon.com/nova/latest/userguide/customize-fine-tune.html |\\n| LLM-SM-TRAIN-005 | Security | HIGH | Job `Failed` with an access error \u2014 the training/customization execution role cannot read the training-data or recipe S3 location, or cannot write the output path (`AccessDenied`, assume-role failure, or an `s3:GetObject`/`PutObject` denial in `FailureReason`). | Grant the execution role least-privilege `s3:GetObject` on the input/recipe prefixes and `s3:PutObject` on the output prefix (and KMS decrypt if the data is CMK-encrypted); verify the trust policy allows `sagemaker.amazonaws.com`. Report the role by name/ARN with the account segment masked. | https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/sagemaker-roles.html |\\n| LLM-SM-TRAIN-006 | Reliability | HIGH | Job `Failed`/produced nothing because an input data channel is empty or points at the wrong S3 URI \u2014 `DescribeTrainingJob` `InputDataConfig` references a prefix with no objects, a wrong bucket/prefix, or a `ContentType`/channel name the recipe does not expect. | Correct the channel `S3Uri`, content type, and channel name to match the recipe\\'s expected inputs; confirm the prefix actually contains the training objects before resubmitting. | https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/your-algorithms-training-algo-running-container.html |\\n| LLM-SM-TRAIN-007 | Reliability | MEDIUM | Job is `InProgress` with `SecondaryStatus` `Starting`/`Pending` waiting on GPU capacity for an extended period \u2014 this is **NOT** `Failed`. {"id": "03f97baf-5b45-4a4e-90a1-ea7193919df8", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "I couldn't find your job. There are no SageMaker training jobs in us-east-1 from the last 7 days in the account this agent space covers. The job may be in another region or account, or older than that. If you send me the job name and region, I can check its actual status.

The status and error message will tell you which problem it is.

| What you see | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Status `InProgress`, secondary status `Starting` or `Pending` | The job is waiting for GPU capacity. It hasn't failed. | Wait. Or stop the job and retry on another instance type or region. Don't change the config or request a quota increase. |
| `Failed` with `InsufficientInstanceCapacity` | **Capacity problem.** AWS has no GPUs of that type available right now. | Retry with backoff, use a different GPU instance type, or try another region. A quota increase won't help. |
| `Failed` with `ResourceLimitExceeded`, or the quota value is 0 | **Quota problem.** Your account's limit for that instance type is too low. | Request a quota increase. Retrying won't help. |

Here is how to confirm which one you have:

1. **Read the job state and failure message.**
   ```
   aws sagemaker describe-training-job --training-job-name <name> --region <region> \
     --query '{Status:TrainingJobStatus,Secondary:SecondaryStatus,Reason:FailureReason,Instance:ResourceConfig.InstanceType,Count:ResourceConfig.InstanceCount}'
   ```
2. **Check your quota for that instance type.** In Service Quotas, look for "`<instance type>` for training job usage", for example `ml.p4d.24xlarge for training job usage`.
   ```
   aws service-quotas list-service-quotas --service-code sagemaker --region <region> \
     --query "Quotas[?contains(QuotaName,'training job usage') && contains(QuotaName,'<instance type>')].{Name:QuotaName,Code:QuotaCode,Value:Value}"
   ```
3. **If the quota value is 0, or lower than your instance count, request an increase.**
   ```
   aws service-quotas request-service-quota-increase --service-code sagemaker \
     --quota-code <code> --desired-value <n> --region <region>
   ```

- **Check the quota first if the job fails immediately:** GPU instance types often default to a quota of 0, and the quota is per instance type and per region.
- **Check for a different failure:** If the job failed without a capacity or quota message, the cause may be something else. Common ones are `iam:PassRole` permissions, S3 or KMS access, or an empty input channel.
- **Don't expect a quota increase to fix a capacity error:** If you hit capacity, a higher quota won't add GPUs.
- **Billing:** You're billed for GPU time only once the job actually starts, not while it waits in `Pending`.

Send me the job name, region and instance type and I'll tell you which case you're in. I only read your account and never change anything, so you'd run the quota request yourself.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
